hints.content:
###The strategy

$\text{Area of a triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \text{base} \cdot \text{height}$

Before we can apply the formula to find the area of $\triangle ABC$, we must find the base and height of the triangle using the Pythagorean theorem (or the distance formula).

* The base is the length $AB$.
* The height is the length $CD$ (the base and the height always meet at a right angle).

###Step 1: Find the length $AB$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
AB^2&= {\redE{2}^2 +\redE{6}^2 }  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
AB&= \sqrt{\redE{2}^2 +\redE{6}^2 }  &&\text{Square root both sides}\\\\
&=\sqrt{40} \\\\
&=\sqrt{4\cdot10} \\\\
&=\tealE{2\sqrt{10}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Triangle A B C has point A at negative four, negative six, point B at two, negative eight, and point C at negative six, negative two. There is a slanted dashed line connecting from point C to a point D at negative seven, negative five and a dashed line connects from point A to point D. The dashed lines make triangle A B C a right triangle at B C D. A vertical line connects two units from point A to a horizontal line of six units connecting to B.

hints.content:
###Step 2: Find the length $CD$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
CD^2&= \redE{3}^2 +\redE{1}^2  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
CD&= \sqrt{\redE{3}^2 +\redE{1}^2 } &&\text{Square root both sides} \\\\
&=\goldE{\sqrt{10}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Triangle A B C has point A at negative four, negative six, point B at two, negative eight, and point C at negative six, negative two. There is a slanted dashed line connecting from point C to a point D at negative seven, negative five and a dashed line connects from point A to point D. The dashed lines make triangle A B C a right triangle at B C D. A vertical line connects three units from point D to a horizontal line of one unit connecting to point C.

hints.content:
###Step 3: Find the area of the triangle

Using the base and height of $\triangle ABC$, we can find the area:

$\begin{align} \text{Area of a triangle} &= \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \text{base} \cdot \text{height}\\\\
&= \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot CD \\\\
&= \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot(\tealE{2\sqrt{10}})\cdot(\goldE{\sqrt{10}}) \\\\
&= \sqrt{10}\cdot\sqrt{10} \\\\
&= 10
\end{align}$

###The answer:

The area of $\triangle ABC$ is $10$ units$^2$.

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Yes, we can find the area of the outer rectangle, then subtract the areas of the triangular and square regions outside of $\triangle ABC$.



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_{\triangle ABC} &= 8(6) - \text{Area}_{\triangle1} - \text{Area}_{\triangle2} - \text{Area}_{\triangle3} - \text{Area}_{\text{square}} \\\\
&=48 - \dfrac{1}{2}(6)(2)-\dfrac{1}{2}(8)(6)-\dfrac{1}{2}(2)(4)- (2)(2)\\\\
&=48 - 6-24-4-4\\\\
&=10
\end{align}$

The area of $\triangle ABC$ is $10$ units$^2$.

A vertical line connects two units from point A to a horizontal line of six units connecting to point B making triangle one. A vertical line connects six units from point B to a horizontal line of eight units connecting to C labeled triangle two. A vertical line connects four units from point C to a horizontal line of two units connecting to A labeled triangle three. A two-by-two square shares the two unit side of triangle three and the two unit side of triangle one. Triangle one, triangle two, triangle three, triangle A B C, and the square create a rectangle with a length of six units and a width of eight units.
